summary.oneLiner: Radiant delivered stable FY25 growth driven by Acemoney's 530% revenue surge and cost discipline, with margins improving despite muted core cash business; the key shift is the strategic pivot toward high-growth fintech and valuables logistics as new profit engines, reducing reliance on volatile BFSI cash flows.

one-line thesis: Radiant delivered stable FY25 growth driven by Acemoney's 530% revenue surge and cost discipline, with margins improving despite muted core cash business; the key shift is the strategic pivot toward high-growth fintech and valuables logistics as new profit engines, reducing reliance on volatile BFSI cash flows.
financial scorecard: revenue: +10.6% YoY; EBITDA/margin: +12.5% YoY, 17.9% (improved 31 bps); PAT (rptd): +5.8% YoY; PAT (normalized): +15% YoY (ex-RVL losses); order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR80cr cash balance, net debt negative
guidance: revenue growth: mid- to high-teens CAGR (15-18%) over next 3 years; margin: aspiration to return to 20%+ EBITDA margins; order inflow: target 90,000 POS machines in FY26; capex/commissioning: incremental capex for RVL pan-India scaling post-lane validation
segment / subsidiary detail: Cash Van Operations: +40% revenue growth; Direct Clients: 15% of revenue (up from 5.2%); Acemoney: INR219cr revenue, 20%+ EBITDA margin, 64,228 POS installed; RVL: <1% revenue, breakeven targeted by Q1FY26; Insta Credit: launched FY25, market reception positive
growth verticals / optionality: Rural fintech penetration (50%+ merchant outlets still cash-only); jewelry logistics market (1.35L jewelers, only 25K serviced); direct B2B cash services to unbanked retail chains; cross-selling Insta Credit to Acemoney merchants
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improvement driven by cost control, Acemoney profitability, and RVL loss reduction; fixed cost leverage under pressure due to muted core revenue growth; RVL costs partially absorbed via shared van/guard infrastructure with RCMS
capex / expansion: Capex focused on Acemoney POS deployment (90K target FY26) and RVL specialized vehicles/software; no major capex beyond incremental scaling; existing cash logistics infrastructure leveraged for RVL
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth in Acemoney and RVL; cash balance of INR80cr provides flexibility for strategic acquisitions; no dividend or buyback mentioned; Acemoney acquisition model (high ROI) as template for future M&A
risks & watch-items: Sluggish BFSI demand (MFI/personal loan); UPI adoption in Tier 4/5; RVL breakeven delay; high fixed cost structure limiting margin expansion without revenue growth; regulatory scrutiny on fintech data security (mitigated by PCI DSS)
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; focused on long-term secular trends (cash-in-circulation, rural digitization); transparent about RVL losses and timeline; optimistic on Acemoney scalability; committed to margin recovery
non-obvious takeaways: Acemoney's transaction-based revenue model (not device sales) creates sticky, scalable unit economics; RVL's 50-50 air/road split leverages existing cash logistics network without new capex; cash loss rates near zero due to ex-service culture, not just tech

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
